why: The only value sent to the addon's set_telemetry_consent sink is a hardcoded False; user_prompt is never used as an argument to any sink.

asset_id/asset_type/resolution/file_format only build a request URL to the trusted api.polyhaven.com and select a dict key; the one caller-adjacent file-write path (extra 'include' files for glTF models, addon.py ~1700) is protected by an effective absolute-path/'..'/prefix check before any file is written to disk.

model_id is URL-quoted before use in the API path and is separately sanitized with re.sub to [A-Za-z0-9_-] before being used as a filename component (addon.py download_polypizza_model); only a single .glb is written, no archive extraction occurs.

uid only selects which Sketchfab-hosted model zip is fetched via the official API; before extractall, addon.py checks every zip member's normalized absolute path against the temp dir prefix and explicitly rejects any '..' segment, so path traversal in the downloaded archive is blocked.

Arbitrary Python execution inside Blender is this tool's entire declared purpose (docstring: 'Execute arbitrary Python code in Blender'), so bare execution is not itself a finding under the advertised-purpose rule. An opt-in AST allowlist (safe_mode.py, gated by BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE, off by default) further restricts scripts when enabled. I reviewed its dunder/attribute blocklist, the getattr/setattr literal-name requirement, the unrooted-navigation backstop for unresolvable receivers, and the module-value-use anti-laundering check (blocking `x = bpy.ops; x.wm.append(...)`), and found no bypass reaching eval/exec/open/os/subprocess or the blocked bpy.ops.script/handlers/timers/registration surface.

sink: reads raw bytes of any local file path via open(path,'rb'); server.py then base64-encodes the bytes and forwards them as 'images' to the addon's create_rodin_job command, which (MAIN_SITE mode, addon.py create_rodin_job_main_site) multipart-uploads the decoded bytes to the third-party Rodin API at https://hyperhuman.deemos.com/api/v2/rodin
why: input_image_paths is declared as 'The absolute paths of input images' but the code's only check is os.path.exists(i) -- existence, not that the path is inside any expected directory or actually an image. Every path supplied is opened, read in full, base64-encoded, and uploaded to an external third-party service (Rodin/hyperhuman.deemos.com) using the user's own API key. A caller (or a model steered by prompt injection -- exactly the threat model safe_mode.py's own docstring names: 'third-party text ... could steer the model into writing hostile code') can pass e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa or any config file readable by the Blender process and have its contents exfiltrated off-box. This exceeds the advertised 'input image' contract and has no guard beyond existence-checking.
contract: input_image_paths: The **absolute** paths of input images. Even if only one image is provided, wrap it into a list.

sink: when input_image_url does not match ^https?://, addon.py's create_hunyuan_job_main_site (OFFICIAL_API mode) opens it as a local file path with open(image,'rb'), base64-encodes it, and POSTs it as ImageBase64 to Tencent Cloud's ai3d SubmitHunyuanTo3DProJob API; create_hunyuan_job_local_site (LOCAL_API mode, addon.py:3499) does the same and posts to a configured local /generate endpoint
why: server.py forwards input_image_url unchanged as 'image' to the addon's create_hunyuan_job command. The only branching logic in addon.py is a regex test for an http(s) scheme; anything else is treated as a local filesystem path with no directory confinement, extension check, or content validation, then its raw bytes are read and shipped to a third-party cloud API (or a local endpoint). Same exfiltration mechanism and same lack of guard as generate_hyper3d_model_via_images's input_image_paths.
contract: input_image_url: (Optional) The local or remote url of the input image. Accepts None if only using text prompt.

why: text_prompt and the numerically-validated bbox_condition (via _process_bbox, which rejects non-positive values) are only forwarded as form/JSON fields to Rodin's own API (hyperhuman.deemos.com or fal.run) using the caller's own configured API key; no path, command, or query surface.
user_prompt is the only caller-supplied value and it is only used as elicitation-prompt/telemetry context text; it never reaches a file, command, URL-path, or query sink.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); the tool only forwards a fixed get_hunyuan3d_status command to the addon, which reports enabled/disabled state.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); the tool only forwards a fixed get_hyper3d_status command to the addon.
object_name is only used as a lookup key in bpy.data.objects.get(name); the result is read-only scene introspection (location/rotation/scale/materials/mesh stats), no file, command, or network sink.

asset_type is validated against a fixed allowlist (['hdris','textures','models','all']) in addon.py get_polyhaven_categories before being interpolated into the api.polyhaven.com request path; invalid values are rejected before the request is made.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); only forwards a fixed get_polyhaven_status command to the addon.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); only forwards a fixed get_polypizza_status command to the addon.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond the required user_prompt (unused as a sink); returns read-only scene/object summary data from bpy.context.scene.

uid selects which Sketchfab-hosted model's info/thumbnail is fetched via the official api.sketchfab.com endpoints using the caller's own API key; the thumbnail URL itself comes from Sketchfab's own API response, not the caller, and the destination host is fixed.
No caller-controlled arguments beyond user_prompt (unused as a sink); only forwards a fixed get_sketchfab_status command to the addon.

The screenshot filepath is built server-side from tempfile.gettempdir() and os.getpid() only; max_size (caller-controlled int) is passed through to Blender's own screenshot-resize logic with no path/command role.

name/task_uuid/request_id are only used as: name -> a Blender object rename (obj.name = name), and task_uuid/request_id -> parameters to Hyper3D's own download/status API (hyperhuman.deemos.com or fal.run) using the caller's own API key; the actual GLB URL downloaded comes from that trusted API's own response, not the caller.

sink: requests.get(zip_file_url, stream=True) fetches any URL with an http/https scheme directly from the Blender addon process; the response is written to disk and imported as glTF (or, for the .zip/.obj fallback branch, extracted with a zip-slip check and imported as OBJ)
guard: partial: addon.py's import_generated_asset_hunyuan_ai only checks re.match(r'^https?://', zip_file_url) -- a bare scheme check. There is no allow-list restricting the host to Tencent's own result-file CDN, so the tool's own contract ('A model URL from ResultFile3Ds') is not actually enforced by code.
why: The tool description implies zip_file_url should be a URL returned by a prior Hunyuan3D generation job, but the implementation accepts any caller-supplied http(s) URL and fetches it server-side with no host allowlist and no exclusion of loopback/link-local/internal addresses -- classic SSRF surface reachable from a process that also holds Tencent Cloud credentials in memory. I could not confirm from static reading alone which internal endpoints would actually be reachable or what a real exploit would return (would require live network testing, which this audit forbids), so I am not claiming a proven exploit -- only a real mechanism with a plausible but unconfirmed impact, which is why this stays Tier B rather than A.
contract: zip_file_url: A model URL from ResultFile3Ds. Prefer a .glb URL when available; .zip/.obj URLs still work as a fallback.

why: job_id is only forwarded as a parameter to the addon's poll_hunyuan_job_status command, which reports Tencent Cloud job status using the caller's own credentials; no path/command/injection surface.

subscription_key/request_id are only forwarded to Hyper3D's own status API (hyperhuman.deemos.com POST body, or interpolated into a fal.run URL path segment) using the caller's own API key; worst case is calling a different endpoint on the same fixed, already-authorized third-party host.

feedback is validated against a fixed enum before use; correction_text/step_index/user_prompt are only placed as length-capped fields inside a structured JSON payload POSTed to Supabase via trajectory.py's _enqueue_row/_post_row -- no string concatenation into a command, path, or query, and no unstructured log line that could break parsing.

asset_type is validated against a fixed allowlist (['hdris','textures','models']) before being placed in the request; categories is passed through requests' own params= dict (properly URL-encoded), not string-concatenated into the URL.

category/licence are resolved through _polypizza_category_id/_polypizza_licence_id, which raise ValueError for anything outside the known name/id sets; the free-text query is percent-encoded with urllib.parse.quote before being placed in the URL path.

query/categories/count/downloadable are placed into requests' own params= dict for a GET to the fixed api.sketchfab.com/v3/search endpoint using the caller's own API key; requests handles encoding, no string-built URL or command.

object_name and texture_id are only used as lookup keys (bpy.data.objects.get, and a startswith() match over already-loaded bpy.data.images names); no file, command, or network sink is reachable from either argument.
